title: Span classes that define __getitem__ must also set __iter__ = None
answers: iter(span) succeeds on a span and then fails when iterated
"name" in span gives a confusing 'not subscriptable' error
span is treated as a sequence by Python
body:
Invariant: any span class that defines __getitem__ must also set `__iter__ = None` next to it.
Why: defining __getitem__ alone enables Python's legacy sequence iteration protocol, so iter(span) returns an iterator that only raises on first use, and `x in span` falls back to that iterator and reports the subscript message.
Enforced at: mlflow/entities/span.py:Span (class attributes __iter__ = None and __getitem__, which always raises TypeError).
If skipped: iteration and membership tests on spans fail with misleading errors instead of the clear 'not iterable' TypeError.
Tests: tests/entities/test_span.py:test_span_is_not_iterable asserts both iter(span) and `"name" in span` raise 'not iterable'.
Applies: Span, LiveSpan, LazySpan and any span-like wrapper in mlflow/entities/span.py that adds __getitem__.
applies: Span-family classes in mlflow/entities/span.py; not for unrelated containers in other modules.
says: Checking if a property exists in a trace span shows a confusing subscript error message.
Looping through a trace span gives a confusing indexing message instead of an iterable warning.
Membership tests on trace spans should clearly report that spans do not support iteration.
Searching inside a trace step should return a clear error stating it is not a sequence.
Trace steps in custom evaluation scripts produce confusing error messages when accessed like a list.
search: Span-family classes in `mlflow/entities/span.py` defining `__getitem__` must also set `__iter__ = None`. Without setting `__iter__ = None`, Python falls back to legacy sequence iteration, causing `iter(span)` to fail only on first consumption and membership checks (`x in span`) to raise misleading subscript errors. `Span`, `LiveSpan`, `LazySpan`, and related wrappers must raise a clear non-iterable TypeError rather than an indexing error. This applies strictly to span-like classes in `mlflow/entities/span.py` and is verified by `tests/entities/test_span.py:test_span_is_not_iterable`.
